accuracy.evidence: Checked for getting lost: stop rather than wander, go to a person who works there at the till or checkout, never go out to the parking lot (NCMEC KidSmartz lost-in-a-store tips); a mother with children as a safe stranger and staying in one place (Kidpower); keep asking until heard (DfE Relationships Education 2019). The adult text says most adults will help, so strangers are not painted as dangerous.

misconceptions.evidence: Predictions target running off to look and going with a kind-sounding person who claims to know where Mum is; wrong turns in every step cover hiding, the car park or gate, asking a dog, giving no names, wandering off alone, running ahead and hide and seek in a shop, the slips named in the adult text.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is a lost-child scene: three places to stop and stay in, a shop where the child is dragged to a person (till worker, mum and child, police officer versus car park door, dog, boxes), a helper who asks who you are, and offers to go off; it is about getting lost and only works for this topic.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner chooses first and the reply explains: running off says you get harder to find, the door says cars are outside and your grown-up looks inside, a wristband answer shows how the helper calls Mum; the step texts confirm the rule (Lost? Stop. Stay inside. Ask a safe helper) after the choice.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: run and look for Mum (the stop step then shows staying is right), someone outside in the car park as a helper (the shop scene shows the door is a wrong turn), and going with a kind man (the stay step shows the reply never go off with anyone).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with its own slip (run, out, hide, go, dog, off, alone, ahead, seek, sweets); for example choosing Go with him gives the reply never go off with anyone, even if they say they know your grown-up.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and everyday words (stop, stay, till, name badge, wristband) and passes the kid readability limit in validate_lessons; adult text names the PSHE and DfE sources and key words in plain language.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph gives one action (stop and stay, find a helper, say who you are, stay with the helper); adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, the evidence behind the advice, the common mistakes and what the lab does, with no repeated template text.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark themes: answer tiles fill the width in one column, the shop scene labels are short and wrapped to two lines, the tray buttons are full size and nothing is clipped at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button in the tray (choices, helpers, answers, ready items); the canvas aria-label is updated with each reply; walk.cjs reports axe clean in both themes on desktop and phone with every Show me task completing.

sources: NCMEC KidSmartz, safety tips: if you get lost in a store go to a checkout counter or an employee, never go to the parking lot
Kidpower International, What to do if you get lost: stay in one place, ask a safe stranger such as a person at a counter or a mother with children
PSHE Association Programme of Study for PSHE Education (2020), Key Stage 1 Health and wellbeing: Keeping safe
DfE (2019) Relationships Education, RSE and Health Education statutory guidance: Being safe
